title: hotfix: SLO enforcement tightening, circuit breaker + regional failover improvements
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Hotfix: tighten SLO enforcement thresholds, fix circuit breaker edge case causing regional failover not triggering, and adjust load-shedding policy to prefer graceful degradation. No breaking changes.
description:
Context: customers observed intermittent request storms in eu-west resulting in downstream queues filling and our regional failover not triggering in a narrow race condition. This resulted in transient ~10% error-rate spikes for high-priority tenants during PG rolling updates. This hotfix tightens SLO enforcement, fixes a circuit-breaker edge case where autoscale state could race with breaker evaluation, and adjusts load-shedding to prefer prefix-KV cache hits and lightweight fallbacks (retries->cached-response->probabilistic-shed).

Changes included (summary):
- SLO enforcement: reduce window for breach detection from 60s->30s for high-priority routes and add hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping. Also add explicit tagging for routes that must always trigger failover on sustained CPU/GPU latency degradation.
- Circuit breaker: fix race in BreakerManager where a node could be marked healthy during an in-flight evaluation and skip failover. Introduced atomic state transitions and a short "pending" state during probe.
- Load-shedding: introduce a priority-aware shedding policy that prefers returning a cached shorter response or structured 503 with retry-after for non-critical tenants. Added a probabilistic shedding knob controlled via config for burst scenarios.
- Regional failover: ensure failover decisions consult both local breaker state and global routing hints; add a conservative cooldown (15s) to avoid oscillation.
- Telemetry & alerts: improve SLO metric tagging (route_priority, failure_mode), add a dashboard for quick incident triage, and create an alert that triggers when failover attempts exceed threshold without success.
- Tests & rollback: unit + integration tests for the breaker state machine and failover path. Rollout plan includes dark-launching the tighter enforcement on 10% of traffic for 2h before full rollout and an automated rollback hook if error rate > 2x baseline.

Why this is hotfix: the race condition allowed a narrow window where regional failover would not trigger causing degraded customer experience during load spikes. The changes are limited, well-tested, and revertible; we want them in main ASAP.

Checklist:
- [x] Reproduced issue in perf-canary with synthetic storm
- [x] Added unit tests for BreakerManager state transitions
- [x] Added integration test simulating region outage and verifying failover
- [x] Metrics added and Grafana dashboard updated
- [x] Canary rollout plan documented
- [x] Verified no regressions in hot-path with local perf runs

Testing performed:
- Local unit + integration: full pass
- Perf-canary: simulated 10k rps burst with mixed priorities; expected failover observed and error-rate stayed within SLOs after change
- Staging rollout (10%): monitored for 3 hours, no regressions; CI re-run green

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main and deploy to staging A (already done for validation)
2) Dark-launch enforcement on 10% traffic in us-east for 2 hours
3) Promote to 50% and monitor SLOs/alerts for 1h
4) Full rollout globally if no regressions or trigger automated rollback

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- ENG-4899: Add a small telemetry sample to trace breaker-probe latency across regions
- SRE-229: Tweak probabilistic-shed parameter per-customer as part of traffic shaping

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the default (global) window conservative; only high-priority routes get the 30s window by default. Ops can flip additional routes via route config if needed.
